key_insight: BrainWideBench introduces a standardized way to test whether large-scale neural pretraining can produce representations that transfer across animals and brain regions. The key idea is to move beyond single-task, single-dataset evaluation and measure general-purpose neural features at scale.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of unified benchmarks for evaluating cross-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings. Existing evaluations are fragmented, making it hard to tell whether bigger neural datasets actually lead to broadly transferable models.
method: Build a benchmark for across-animal transfer using multi-region neural recordings.
Evaluate pretrained models on diverse downstream tasks instead of a narrow task domain.
Compare how well representations learned from large-scale pretraining transfer across animals, brain regions, and experimental settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer and more realistic testbed for learning reusable neural representations. It can guide model design, training objectives, and dataset scaling decisions for neuroscience-informed machine learning.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multi-animal, multi-region recordings flowing into pretraining and downstream transfer tasks.
A benchmark leaderboard chart comparing models across tasks and animals.
An icon-based map of brain regions and animals to illustrate cross-domain transfer.
A matrix heatmap showing transfer performance between source animals/regions and target tasks.
paper_title: BrainWideBench: Benchmarking large-scale pretraining and across-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings
paper_authors: Alexandre Andre, Shivashriganesh P. Mahato, Vinam Arora, Keshav Balaji, Divyansha Lachi
